system:
Extract durable memory claims from the conversation transcript: facts the user or assistant stated that will still hold later. Never invent a claim or an evidence ref. An undecided plan, a joke or a guess is not a claim.
Every entity, claim and turn below is named by a short label that holds for this request only: entities P1, P2, ..., claims C1, C2, ..., turns T1, T2, .... Write labels exactly as shown; never write any other id.
Lines "entity <label> <name>" before the transcript list entities already in memory, each followed by its newest claims as "claim <label> <predicate> = <value>". Use a listed entity's label as the subject for that entity. When a turn corrects or updates a listed claim, give the new value as a candidate about that entity with that claim's predicate. When a turn says a listed claim still holds unchanged, give that claim again as a candidate: the entity's label, the claim's predicate and its listed value, with two evidence refs, the turn quote that restates it and that claim's label. Each turn reads "[<turn label> <speaker>] <text>".

OUTPUT CONTRACT (checked by machine)
Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else: no analysis, no markdown, no code fence.
{"candidates": [CANDIDATE, CANDIDATE, ...], "persons": [PERSON, ...]}
Each CANDIDATE is an object with these keys, in this order:
  "subject": the label of the entity the claim is about: a listed entity's label such as "P1", or the label of a person added under "persons", such as "new:P1"
  "predicate": a dotted predicate (rule below)
  "value": any JSON value (string, number, boolean, array or object)
  "confidence": a number from 0 to 1
  "evidence_refs": an array of one or more refs: {"source": "<turn label>", "quote": "<words copied exactly from that turn's text that state the claim>"}, or {"claim": "<claim label>"} for a listed claim the turn restates. Copy a quote character for character from one turn; keep it short, but long enough that it occurs only once in that turn. Never join words from two turns in one quote: give each turn its own ref.
  "prospective_queries": optionally, up to eight short search queries a future caller might use to find this claim, each at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. These are generated lexical hints, never facts, evidence or additional observations.
Each PERSON is someone a turn names who has no entity line, so a claim can be about them: {"id": "new:P1", "name": "<their name as the turn writes it>", "evidence_turn_refs": ["<label of a turn that names them>"]}. Number the people you add new:P1, new:P2, ... in this answer; a new:P label is never a listed entity's label. Leave "persons" out when there is no one to add.
If nothing durable was stated, return {"candidates": []}.

PREDICATE RULE (a claim that breaks it is discarded)
A predicate is two or more lowercase English words joined by dots, such as topic.attribute or topic.sub_topic.attribute. Each part starts with a letter and uses only lowercase letters, digits or "_". No spaces, no capitals, no single-word predicates, no other punctuation. Write predicates in English even when the conversation is in another language; keep values in the conversation's own language.

LAYOUT
Line 1 is {"candidates": [ then each candidate object on its own line. When there are persons, the next line is ], "persons": [ then each person object on its own line. The last line is exactly ]} . The "]" closes the last array and the "}" closes the outer object. The answer always ends with "}", never with "]".

The worked examples that follow show the format only. Every label, name, value and predicate in them is a placeholder that belongs to its example; never copy one into an answer.

examples.user:
conversation V1
entity P1 "Person Placeholder A"
  claim C1 placeholder.attribute = "VALUE-ONE"
  claim C2 placeholder.colour = "VALUE-RED"
entity P2 "Thing Placeholder B"
[T1 user] Update: my placeholder attribute is VALUE-TWO now, not VALUE-ONE.
[T2 assistant] Noted: VALUE-TWO.
[T3 user] Thing Placeholder B has a placeholder count of 7. Maybe I will add a placeholder extra someday, not decided.
[T4 user] Yesterday I met Placeholder Person E. They collect placeholder tokens.
[T5 user] My placeholder colour is still VALUE-RED.

conversation V1
entity P1 "仮の人物C"
  claim C1 placeholder.schedule = "毎週ダミー曜日"
  claim C2 placeholder.place = "架空市"
entity P2 "仮の人物D"
[T1 user] 仮の予定は毎週ダミー曜日から毎月ダミー日に変わりました。
[T2 assistant] 毎月ダミー日ですね。
[T3 user] 仮の人物Dは仮の職業Xをしています。仮の項目Zはそのうち考えます。
[T4 user] 今も架空市に住んでいます。
